elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause 4(a): "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right (no Order Form structure exists in this MSA).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The retained/edited notice period for Customer is ninety (90) days, not 30; and the right is unavailable during the one-year Initial Term ("Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b)").

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic anywhere in 4(a); the opposite is retained — "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement". To meet this element the drafter would need an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Edited sentence: "Kubient may terminate on such notice only effective at the end of the then-current Term", read with the retained bar on any termination during the Initial Term; the effective date is expressly tied to term end, so no mid-term Vendor convenience exit remains.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band; the Initial Term carve-out is a mutual restriction on a 12-month term and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed on Customer. The only retained payment mechanic is "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — for a Customer convenience exit that period is the 90-day notice window (i.e. no more than three months, and in fact fees actually generated in the ordinary revenue-share course, not a penalty). The cap condition is therefore not exceeded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "Kubient may terminate on such notice only effective at the end of the then-current Term" expressly ties the effective date to term end, curing the pre-edit mutual mid-term for-any-reason exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "on such notice" refers back to the immediately preceding "ninety (90) days written notice", so Kubient's term-end convenience termination carries the same 90-day notice requirement.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (90-day Customer exit, no early-termination fee above three months, Vendor convenience exit expressly effective only at the end of the then-current Term, on the same 90 days' notice).

Preferred is not reached: Customer's notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — the retained sentence entitling Kubient to all fees generated during the termination period runs the other way. If the drafter wants the preferred level, it must add an express 30-day Customer notice and a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund.

'Deviation' is the correct pre-edit status: the original sentence let Kubient terminate for any reason mid-renewal-term on 90 days' notice, which fails the fallback element requiring a term-end-only Vendor convenience right; it is not walk-away territory because Customer had a convenience right and Vendor's notice was not under 90 days.

Minimal: the change is confined to splitting the single mutual sentence into party-specific limbs and tying Kubient's effective date to term end. The Customer limb, the Initial Term bar, the material-breach and insolvency provisions and the fees-during-termination sentence are all retained verbatim. Drafting nit (not a minimality failure but worth repairing): the phrase "to the other Party" was dropped from the Customer limb, leaving the notice recipient implicit — restore as "written notice to Kubient".

Preserves intent: no dangling cross-references or undefined terms; "then-current Term" draws on the defined "Term". One residual reading point — because Kubient's termination now takes effect at term end, the retained "all fees generated during the termination period" could span a longer window for a Kubient-initiated exit, but those are fees actually generated under the revenue-share model, so no contradiction with the retained commercial mechanic.
